description: Four-panel composite of tensile behaviour of three austenitic low-density steels: 28Mn0Ni (black), 28Mn5Ni (red) and 15Mn5Ni (blue). (a) Engineering stress (MPa, axis 0-2000) versus engineering strain (0.00-0.12) in HR + CR condition; the blue 15Mn5Ni curve peaks highest (just above the 1750 MPa level) but terminates near 0.06 strain, whereas the black and red curves peak at roughly 1450-1550 MPa with 28Mn5Ni reaching ~0.12 strain. (b) Engineering stress-strain after HR + CR + heat treatment, with the strain axis expanded to 0.0-0.9 and seven labelled curves (28Mn0Ni at 973 K, 1023 K, 1173 K; 28Mn5Ni at 973 K, 1023 K, 1173 K; 15Mn5Ni-1173 K); the solid black 28Mn0Ni-1173 K curve attains ~0.85 strain near 900 MPa. (c) True stress (0-2000 MPa) versus true strain (0.0-0.6) for five heat-treated conditions; the blue 15Mn5Ni-1173 K and red 28Mn5Ni-1173 K curves overlap closely, reaching ~1700-1800 MPa, while solid black 28Mn0Ni-1173 K is lowest and most gradual. (d) ln(σ) versus ln(ε) (y 6.0-7.6, x -6 to 0) with slope triangles annotated 0.16, 0.3 and 0.5 (strain-hardening exponents n). Together the panels show that cold rolling gives high strength/low ductility, that heat treatment restores ductility, and that the Ni-free alloy hardens most.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa) versus engineering strain (0.00-0.12) for the HR + CR (50% cold reduction) condition, with legend 28Mn0Ni (black), 28Mn5Ni (red), 15Mn5Ni (blue). All three rise steeply to ~1450-1800 MPa within ~0.02 strain with negligible strain hardening; the blue 15Mn5Ni curve is highest and terminates earliest (~0.06 strain), the red 28Mn5Ni extends furthest (~0.12 strain).

Engineering stress (MPa) versus engineering strain (0.0-0.9) for HR + CR + heat treated conditions; seven curves: 28Mn0Ni-973 K (dashed black), 28Mn0Ni-1023 K (dash-dot black), 28Mn0Ni-1173 K (solid black), 28Mn5Ni-973 K (dashed red), 28Mn5Ni-1023 K (dash-dot red), 28Mn5Ni-1173 K (solid red), 15Mn5Ni-1173 K (solid blue). The solid black 28Mn0Ni-1173 K curve reaches the largest strain (~0.85) at the lowest stress level (~900 MPa); the dashed red 28Mn5Ni-973 K shows the highest stress (~1500-1550 MPa) but limited strain.

True stress (MPa, 0-2000) versus true strain (0.0-0.6) for selected heat treated conditions with the same legend scheme as (b). The blue 15Mn5Ni-1173 K and red 28Mn5Ni-1173 K curves overlap and rise to ~1700-1800 MPa by ~0.33 true strain; the dashed/dash-dot black 28Mn0Ni-973 K and -1023 K curves lie above the solid black 28Mn0Ni-1173 K curve, which is the lowest and rises most gradually to ~1500 MPa near 0.55 strain.

ln(σ) (axis 6.0-7.6) versus ln(ε) (axis -6 to 0) for the same heat-treated conditions as (c), with three triangular slope markers annotated 0.16, 0.3 and 0.5. All curves show two-slope behaviour; the 0.5 triangle sits on the 28Mn0Ni-1173 K solid black curve, the 0.3 triangle between the red and blue 1173 K curves, and the 0.16 triangle near the dash-dot black curve (labelled 28Mn0Ni-1023 K in the legend).

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots engineering stress (MPa, 0-2000) against engineering strain (0.00-0.12) with the internal label 'HR+CR' and legend 28Mn0Ni (black), 28Mn5Ni (red), 15Mn5Ni (blue).

In panel (a) the 15Mn5Ni (blue) curve reaches the highest stress (above the 1750 MPa level) but terminates at the lowest strain (~0.06), while 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni plateau at ~1450-1550 MPa with 28Mn5Ni extending to ~0.12 strain.

Panel (b) uses a much wider strain axis (0.0-0.9) than panel (a) and contains seven curves labelled with heat treatment temperatures 973 K, 1023 K and 1173 K for 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni plus 15Mn5Ni-1173 K only.

In panel (b) the solid black curve 28Mn0Ni-1173 K attains the largest tensile strain (~0.85) but at the lowest stress level (~850-900 MPa), whereas the dashed red curve 28Mn5Ni-973 K reaches ~1500-1550 MPa at small strain and ends near 0.2 strain.
No engineering stress-strain curves for 15Mn5Ni heat treated at 973 K or 1023 K appear in panels (b) or (c); only the 15Mn5Ni-1173 K curve (blue) is plotted.
In panel (c) the blue 15Mn5Ni-1173 K and red 28Mn5Ni-1173 K true stress-true strain curves lie nearly on top of one another and reach ~1700-1800 MPa at ~0.33 true strain.

Panel (d) annotates three slope triangles on the ln(σ) versus ln(ε) curves with the values 0.16, 0.3 and 0.5, and all curves show a change of slope (two-slope behaviour) with small exponent at low ln(ε).
The caption states that (c) shows true stress-true strain curves and (d) shows log(σ) versus log(ε) plots for the three alloys in selected heat treated conditions.

The citing text states that all three alloys in HR + CR condition exhibited yield stress (0.2% offset) of 1.35-1.67 GPa and tensile strengths of 1.5-1.8 GPa with limited tensile elongations of 6-11% and negligible strain hardening.

The citing text states that 15Mn5Ni alloy displayed relatively higher strengths and lower ductility among the three alloys in HR + CR, and that uniform strain values in this condition were less than 3% in all alloys.
The citing text states that the maximum tensile elongation to failure of ~86% was attained by 28Mn0Ni in the fully recrystallized and grain growth condition (HR + CR + 1173 K).

The citing text states that upon heat treatment to 973 K and 1023 K the 15Mn5Ni alloy behaved like a brittle material with tensile elongation <1% and its stress-strain curves could not be recorded, whereas 28Mn5Ni was still significantly ductile at those temperatures.

The citing text states that the strain-hardening exponent n of 28Mn0Ni increased from 0.16 to 0.50 with increasing heat treatment temperature from 973 K to 1173 K, while both Ni-containing alloys showed nearly identical n of ~0.30 at 1173 K.

Discrepancy: the citing text attributes n = 0.16 to 28Mn0Ni heat treated at 973 K, but in panel (d) the 0.16 slope triangle is drawn on the dash-dot black curve, which the legend assigns to 28Mn0Ni-1023 K; the 0.5 triangle sits on the 28Mn0Ni-1173 K solid black curve.

The citing text states that yield stress (YS), tensile strength (TS) and total tensile elongation to failure (TE) derived from these stress-strain curves are listed in Table 3, and that n values are also reported there.

measured_quantities: strain-hardening exponent n (slope of ln σ vs ln ε)
unreadable_items: panel (d): the curve assignment of the 0.16 slope triangle is ambiguous — the legend labels the dash-dot black curve 28Mn0Ni-1023 K while the citing text attributes n = 0.16 to the 973 K condition; both readings are reported
panel (d): the 0.3 triangle is not explicitly tied to a single curve in the legend, so which of the red/blue 1173 K curves it measures is not resolvable from the pixels
no printed numeric data values (YS, TS, TE) appear on any panel; these are stated only in the caption/citing text and Table 3
